# Held-Out Error over Training Error

Training error cannot select a model, and the reason is structural rather than statistical: for
nested model families it is **monotonically non-increasing in complexity by construction**.

A degree-`d+1` polynomial can reproduce any degree-`d` one by setting the leading coefficient to
zero. So the best degree-`d+1` fit is at least as good as the best degree-`d` fit, on *any*
data, always. Selecting on training error therefore picks the largest candidate in the list —
and it does so for a reason that has nothing to do with the data.

## The measurement

```
     degree        train   validation
          0      0.47624      0.40153
          1      0.27474      0.24176
          3      0.01360      0.01025
          5      0.00568      0.01165
          7      0.00512      0.01015  <- chosen
          9      0.00264      0.01315
```

Training error falls all the way to degree 9. Validation error does not — it bottoms out and
comes back up, and that **non-monotonicity is the entire product** of holding data out. A split
that produced a monotone validation curve would have bought nothing.

Both facts are assertions in the test suite rather than observations in a comment: the
monotonicity of the training column is asserted, and so is the non-monotonicity of the
validation column.

## The same trap without a degree

Model complexity does not have to be a visible parameter for this to bite.

κ-NN at `k = 1` has zero training error by construction, because every training point is its own
nearest neighbour at distance zero. A `k` chosen on training error is always 1 — again, for
reasons unrelated to the data. See [[lazy-versus-eager-learners]].

The general form: **any metric that a model can drive to its optimum by memorising cannot
distinguish memorising from learning.** Test-set accuracy on a set that was consulted while
tuning has the same defect and is harder to notice.

## The guarantee has a precondition

κ-NN's zero-training-error property holds only while no two identical feature vectors carry
different labels. With a contradictory duplicate, `k = 1` scores 0.8 rather than 1.0 — one of
the two identical points must be wrong whatever the classifier does.

Real text data is full of duplicate feature vectors, so this is not a corner case. It was found
by writing a test that assumed the guarantee and measuring 0.8, which is the useful direction
for a precondition to be discovered in.

## Replacing a discrete search with a continuous one

Once ridge regression is available, the degree stops needing to be guessed correctly: fix a
generously large degree and select λ instead. One continuous parameter replaces one discrete
one and is easier to search — see [[condition-number-as-digits-lost]] for what λ is doing to the
solve while it does that.

## Where this appears

Implemented in [[systems-analysis-and-decision-support]] with both selection sweeps keeping every
candidate they rejected rather than returning only the winner. The wider habit —
[[blind-baseline-comparison]] — is the same argument applied to whether a model beats doing
nothing at all.
